description: The default story demonstrates a basic line chart configuration. The chart is configured via the config property, which accepts an object that maps directly to the ECharts option configuration.
title: Default

description: The config property is the main way to configure the chart. It accepts an object that maps 1:1 to the ECharts option configuration. Assigning a new object to this property will update the chart with the new configuration.
title: Config

description: Use the palette attribute to apply a Synergy design token color palette to chart series. categorical (12 distinct colors for comparing unrelated data series), sequential-01–sequential-07 (10-step single-hue ramps), and sequential-status-critical/error/info/success/warning (10-step status ramps). If option.color is explicitly set, it takes precedence over the palette attribute.
title: Palette

description: Use getInstance() to access the underlying ECharts instance directly and work with its full native API. This is useful when the config property alone is not sufficient — for example to listen to ECharts events, trigger actions, or call setOption() with custom merge behavior. This example attaches a click listener via the native ECharts API. Click any data point to see the event payload logged to the browser console.
title: Get Instance

description: You can use multiple charts in one <syn-chart> instance, each with its own configuration. The palette colors or the default colors can be overridden per series item using the color property directly on the series object — allowing fine-grained control over individual chart series colors.Important: The color property does not support CSS variables (e.g. var(--syn-sequential-05-80)). This is a limitation of ECharts itself: ECharts renders via the Canvas API, which does not resolve CSS custom properties. To use Synergy design tokens as colors, read the computed hex value first using getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--your-token').trim() and pass the resolved value instead.
title: Multiple Charts With Different Palettes

description: The default is, that both axes lines as well as the split lines are hidden.
title: Axes Split Lines Hidden

description: If you want to display both axes lines and split lines, use the handle method axesShowSplitLines().
title: Axes Split Lines Visible

description: To show only horizontal split lines, use the handle method axesShowYSplitLines().
title: Horizontal Split Lines Visible

description: To show only vertical split lines, use the handle method axesShowXSplitLines().
title: Vertical Split Lines Visible

description: If you want to hide the axis labels, use the handle method axesHideLabels().
title: Axes Labels Hidden

description: To show axes split lines but hide axis labels, combine axesShowSplitLines() and axesHideLabels().
title: Axes Lines Visible With Labels Hidden

description: To add icons to axis labels, use the handle methods axesAddXLabelIcons() and axesAddYLabelIcons().
title: Axes Labels With Icons

description: The default position of the y-axis is left and for the x-axis is bottom. The axes can be positioned at the top, bottom, left or right of the chart by using the position option.
title: Axes Positioning

description: The default min and max values of the axes are calculated automatically based on the data. The min and max values can be set manually by using the min and max options for the axes.
title: Min Max Values

description: To add multiple y-axes to the chart, define an array of y-axis configurations under the yAxis option. Shared y-axes are positioned on the left side by default, and you can specify the position for each axis individually.
title: Multiple Y Axes

description: This chart compares two metrics (temperature, precipitation) for two countries (Germany, France) using a single shared axis approach, encoded through visual channels that do not depend on color perception at all: 1. Line style and marker shape = country Germany is drawn with solid lines and filled square/circle markers; France is drawn with dotted lines. This distinction is fully readable in grayscale or black-and-white print, since it relies on stroke pattern and shape rather than hue. 2. Legend labels = explicit redundant encodingRather than expecting the reader to decode line style or marker shape from a key, each legend entry spells out both dimensions in text: "Temperature Germany", "Preciptation France". This turns the legend itself into a self-sufficient lookup table, so no single visual channel has to carry the full weight of disambiguation.Color is still used in this chart (blue/green) to make the two metrics faster to tell apart on screen, but it is treated as a supporting cue only and never as the sole means of distinguishing a series. Every distinction the chart makes is also carried by line style, marker shape, or the legend text, so the chart remains fully legible if color is removed entirely (e.g. printed in black and white, or viewed by a colorblind user).
title: Multiple Series Per Y Axis

description: The axes labels can be formatted via the axisLabel.formatter option. You can customize the formatting to display the labels in a way that best suits your data and visualization needs. We provide predefined formatting functions like unitFormatter, numberFormatter and numberShorthandFormatter.
title: Axes Label Formatting

description: The default behavior of ECharts for justifiying axes labels is to avoid overlapping.This default behavior can hide more labels than necessary even when some space is still available. If you want labels to be placed more greedily, use axisLabel.interval = 0 together with hideOverlap: true. This distributes the available space greedily from left to right on horizontal axes and from top to bottom on vertical axes. If a label does not fit into its slot, the space is released for the next tick, and labels are rendered either completely or not at all. This does only work for axis of type category.
title: Category Axes Label Greedily

description: When all axis labels should remain visible and be distributed evenly along the axis, configure the labels to use a fixed amount of space per tick. If the available space becomes insufficient, labels are automatically truncated. This behavior can be achieved with axisLabel.interval = 0, axisLabel.width (calculated based on the available space per tick), and axisLabel.overflow = 'truncate'. To keep the layout responsive, recalculate the label width on window resize and update the chart configuration accordingly. This does only work for axis of type category.
title: Category Axes Label Evenly

description: The default position of the legend is top. The legend can be positioned at the top of the chart by using the handle method legendShow() or legendShow({ position: 'top' }).
title: Show Legend Top

description: The legend can be positioned at the left of the chart by using the handle method legendShow({ position: 'left' }).
title: Show Legend Left

description: The legend can be positioned at the right of the chart by using the handle method legendShow({ position: 'right' }).
title: Show Legend Right

description: The legend can be positioned at the bottom of the chart by using the handle method legendShow({ position: 'bottom' }).
title: Show Legend Bottom

description: By default, the legend is interactive. Users can click on a legend item to toggle the visibility of the corresponding series in the chart. To make the legend non-interactive, use the selectedMode: false option.
title: Non Interactive Legend

description: Use predefined types like average, min or max as start or endpoints in markArea.data.type.
title: Min Max And Average

description: Add yAxis values to the two points in markArea.data to highlight a horizontal value range across the chart. The area spans the full category axis between the specified values.
title: Value Range

description: Add xAxis category values to the two points in markArea.data to highlight a range of categories. You can define multiple areas to call out separate periods and give each area a name for context.
title: Category Range

description: The label position can be configured using label.position. While multiple positions are supported, 'insideLeft' is recommended for horizontal mark areas and 'insideTop' for vertical mark areas. The default position is 'insideLeft'.
title: Label Position

description: Use Synergy's NAMUR status colors when a highlighted range needs to communicate intent: green for a target that has been met, red for an exceeded limit or critical range, and yellow/orange for a warning. Set the area color in itemStyle and use opacity to keep the data visible beneath it.
title: Intent Colors

description: Use type: 'min' and type: 'max' in markLine.data to highlight the minimum and maximum values of a series.
title: Min And Max

description: Use type: 'average' in markLine.data to show the average value of a series as a reference line.
title: Average

description: Add a yAxis value to markLine.data to draw a horizontal threshold line. Use an xAxis value for a vertical line at a specific category.
title: Fixed Thresholds

description: Define a mark line with a pair of coord points to connect custom coordinates. Configure symbol to control the symbols at either end of the line.
title: Coordinate Line

description: Use Synergy's NAMUR status colors when a reference line needs to communicate intent: green for a target that has been met, red for an exceeded limit or critical threshold and yellow/orange for a warning.
title: Intent Colors

description: The label position can be configured using label.position. While several positions are supported, start and end are generally recommended. To ensure long labels remain fully visible, adjust the chart grid (for example grid.left, grid.top, etc.) to provide sufficient space around the chart area. Use label.formatter to customize the displayed text, such as combining the mark line name with the value.
title: Label Position

description: Hide the label for a mark line by setting label.show to false.
title: No Label

description: Use predefined types like average, min or max as points in markPoint.data.type.
title: Min Max And Average

description: Set coord: [category, value] on each marker to highlight specific data coordinates. Use name for descriptive context and value for the value exposed to label formatters. Coordinates may also use numeric values on value axes.
title: Coordinates

description: Customize individual mark points with symbol, symbolSize, label.position and itemStyle.color. Pair color with distinct shapes and meaningful labels so status remains clear without relying on color alone.
title: Custom Styling

description: By default, mark points use pin-shaped markers with the value shown inside. When a descriptive label is too long to fit in the pin, use a compact symbol such as circle and position the label outside of it.
title: Long Labels

description: When having large data sets or dense series where users need to inspect local trends without leaving the chart context, the dataZoom option with type: 'inside' can be used. It enables direct interaction inside the plotting area: - mouse drag to pan- mouse wheel to zoom There are possibilities to customize the zooming behavior, for example, to restrict zooming to a specific axis, to set minimum and maximum zoom levels or to add an additional key for zooming. For more information have a look at the ECharts documentation
title: Integrated Zooming

description: The data zoom slider (the dataZoom option with type: 'inside') allows users to define a specific data zoom level within a chart by dragging the left and right handles or moving the entire selection bar. It's commonly used in dashboards and analytics tools to filter, zoom, or focus on a subset of data without losing context of the full dataset. The component consists of three interactive elements: - Left handle: Defines the start of the selected zoom- Right handle: Defines the end of the selected zoom- Selection bar (center): Moves the entire zoom without changing its widthThe slider can be customized in terms of position, size and appearance. For more information have a look at the ECharts documentation
title: Slider Zooming

description: An area chart can be configured via the chart config with type: 'line' and areaStyle: {} or with the seriesArea preset function. When using a config object, set areaStyle.opacity to 0.2 for the recommended styling. The seriesArea preset applies this opacity by default. Pass a custom areaStyle to override the preset default.
title: Default

description: The area series supports curved lines. Use the smooth property to enable smooth curves.
title: Curved Line

description: The lines of area series can be hidden. When hidden, only the filled area remains for a more minimal, volume-focused visualization.
title: Hidden Line

description: The line styles can be adjusted such as solid, dashed, and dotted as well as custom line widths. Use distinct styles to differentiate series when needed.
title: Line Styles And Widths

description: The data points can be marked via symbols. Set symbol and symbolSize on each series to customize them.
title: Symbol Styles And Sizes

description: Use the palette attribute to apply another Synergy chart color palette to the area series.
title: Color Palettes

description: By default, each area series is assigned a color from the chart's categorical color palette. Use the colors option to provide explicit colors instead. Colors are repeated cyclically when fewer colors than data points are provided.
title: Custom Colors

description: Area charts can display both positive and negative values, filling each data point relative to the configured area origin.
title: Positive And Negative Values

description: Use the areaStyle.origin option to choose the baseline from which an area is filled. Valid values:- auto fills the area between the axis line and the data (default).- start fills between the minimum axis value and the data.- end fills between the maximum axis value and the data.- A number fills between that specified value and the data.
title: Origin

description: The stack value names a stack group. Area series with the same stack value on the same category axis are stacked on top of one another. Use stackStrategy to control how values are accumulated:- samesign stacks a value only when it has the same sign as the current stack total (default)- all stacks values regardless of whether they are positive or negative- positive stacks only positive values- negative stacks only negative values
title: Stack

description: Set emphasis.focus to series to highlight the hovered area series and de-emphasize the others.
title: Focus On Hover

description: Enable contextual data point details with the tooltipShow() preset. The tooltip displays labels and values as users interact with the chart.
title: Tooltip

description: Use legendShow() to display a legend for named series. Series names become the legend labels, and users can toggle series visibility interactively.
title: With Legend

description: Configure dataZoom to let users focus on a subset of an area chart's data. The slider provides handles for selecting the visible range.
title: Zoom

description: Use the seriesAreaRange preset function to create area range charts. This preset accepts each data point as a pair of lower and upper values and automatically generates the boundary lines, filled area and tooltip configuration. Its optional second argument accepts line series options that are merged into both boundary series and can override their defaults.Alternatively, an area range can be configured using two stacked line series. Both series must use the same stack and name value. The first series contains the lower bound values and has its tooltip disabled. The second series contains the difference between the upper and lower values (upper - lower) and defines an areaStyle to render the shaded range. To display the actual range in the tooltip, format the second series' tooltip value using the original lower and upper values rather than the calculated difference values.
title: Default

description: Set smooth: true to curve the upper and lower boundaries of the range.
title: Curved Line

description: Set lineStyle.width to 0 and configure symbol to show data point markers. When lines are hidden, only the filled range and its markers remain for a more minimal, range-focused visualization.
title: Hidden Line

description: Customize range boundary lines with solid, dashed or dotted styles, and adjust their width. Use distinct styles to differentiate multiple area range series
title: Line Styles And Widths

description: Use symbol and symbolSize to choose the marker shape and size for area range data points. Set symbol to none to hide the markers.
title: Symbol Styles And Sizes

description: Set the chart's palette attribute to apply a Synergy chart color palette to area range series.
title: Color Palettes

description: By default, each series is assigned a color from the chart's categorical color palette. Use the colors option to provide explicit colors instead. Colors are repeated cyclically when fewer colors than data points are provided.
title: Custom Colors

description: Area ranges can cross zero and include both positive and negative values. The chart displays the full lower-to-upper interval for each category.
title: Positive And Negative Values

description: Enable contextual values for area range data points with the tooltipShow() preset. Give each series a name to identify it in the tooltip.
title: Tooltip

description: Use legendShow() to display a legend for named area range series. Users can select legend entries to toggle the corresponding ranges.
title: With Legend

description: A grouped bar chart is created when multiple bar series share the same category axis. The value axis defines the scale for the bar values. The bar chart can be configured via the chart config with type: bar or with the seriesBar preset function.
title: Default

description: Place categories on the x-axis and values on the y-axis, where bar height represents value magnitude. Vertical bar charts work well for chronological trends and smaller category sets, and make differences in magnitude easy to compare.
title: Vertical

description: Place categories on the y-axis and values on the x-axis, where bar length represents value magnitude. Horizontal bar charts are best suited for:- Long category labels: Provides ample horizontal room for text, avoiding overlapping, truncation, or awkward label rotations.- Large datasets: Scales cleanly for 10 or more categories without compressing bar widths.- Rankings: Naturally presents ordered lists (ascending or descending) in a top-to-bottom reading flow.
title: Horizontal

description: Use min and max on the value axis to set explicit scale boundaries. Fixed ranges help standardize comparisons across charts, anchor benchmarks such as 0–100%, provide headroom for labels and tooltips, and prevent scale shifts when data changes.
title: Fixed Value Range

description: Bar charts can show negative values such as deficits, losses, or decreases. Bars extend away from the zero baseline.
title: Negative Values

description: Bar charts can combine positive and negative values to show gains and losses or deviations from a baseline. Bars extend in opposite directions from zero.
title: Positive And Negative

description: Set barWidth to control bar thickness. A number specifies a fixed width in pixels, while a percentage string sets the width relative to the available category space and adapts to the chart size. By default, bars are responsive but capped at 24 px by the theme's barMaxWidth setting. To use bars wider than 24 px, also increase barMaxWidth on the series.
title: Custom Bar Width

description: Bar series use the chart's categorical palette by default. Use the color option to apply explicit colors to individual series.
title: Custom Colors

description: Depending on your use case, choose a categorical palette (up to 12 colors) or a sequential palette (recommended for up to 3 colors).
title: Categorical Vs Sequential

description: Enable a tooltip to inspect bar values on hover. For bar series it is recommended to set tooltip.axisPointer.type to 'shadow' to highlight the corresponding category and compare its values across series.
title: Tooltip

description: Use legendShow() to display a legend for named series. Series names become the legend labels, and users can toggle series visibility interactively.
title: Legend

description: Selection is disabled by default. Set selectedMode to true or 'single' to select one data item at a time, 'multiple' to select multiple data items, or 'series' to select an entire series.
title: Selected Mode

description: The bar chart can be configured via the chart config with type: bar or with the seriesBar preset function.
title: Default

description: Place categories on the x-axis and values on the y-axis, where bar height represents value magnitude. Vertical bar charts work well for chronological trends and smaller category sets, and make differences in magnitude easy to compare.
title: Vertical

description: Place categories on the y-axis and values on the x-axis, where bar length represents value magnitude. Horizontal bar charts are best suited for:- Long category labels: Provides ample horizontal room for text, avoiding overlapping, truncation, or awkward label rotations.- Large datasets: Scales cleanly for 10 or more categories without compressing bar widths.- Rankings: Naturally presents ordered lists (ascending or descending) in a top-to-bottom reading flow.
title: Horizontal

description: Use min and max on the value axis to set explicit scale boundaries. Fixed ranges help standardize comparisons across charts, anchor benchmarks such as 0–100%, provide headroom for labels and tooltips, and prevent scale shifts when data changes.
title: Fixed Value Range

description: Bar charts can show negative values such as deficits, losses, or decreases. Bars extend away from the zero baseline.
title: Negative Values

description: Bar charts can combine positive and negative values to show gains and losses or deviations from a baseline. Bars extend in opposite directions from zero.
title: Positive And Negative

description: Set barWidth to control bar thickness. A number specifies a fixed width in pixels, while a percentage string sets the width relative to the available category space and adapts to the chart size. By default, bars are responsive but capped at 24 px by the theme's barMaxWidth setting. To use bars wider than 24 px, also increase barMaxWidth on the series.
title: Custom Bar Width

description: Bar series use the chart's categorical palette by default. Use the color option to apply explicit colors to individual series.
title: Custom Colors

description: Enable a tooltip to inspect bar values on hover. For bar series it is recommended to set tooltip.axisPointer.type to 'shadow' to highlight the corresponding category and compare its values across series.
title: Tooltip

description: Selection is disabled by default. Set selectedMode to true or 'single' to select one data item at a time, 'multiple' to select multiple data items, or 'series' to select an entire series.
title: Selected Mode

description: Set large: true to enable optimized rendering when a bar series contains many data points. The optimization is used once the number of items reaches largeThreshold (400 by default). Individual data-item styles cannot be customized while large rendering is active, so use it when rendering performance matters more than per-item styling.
title: Large Data Set

description: Configure a stacked bar chart with type: 'bar' and a shared stack identifier or use the seriesBarStacked preset function. Showing labels is recommended and their color should inherit the series color. Place labels to the left for vertical bars and above for horizontal bars. A 1 px border is recommended to better distinguish adjacent bar segments. The seriesBarStacked preset applies these label and border settings by default. It also sets barCategoryGap to control the spacing between category groups and barMinWidth to keep bars from becoming too narrow. These defaults help maintain readability, but cannot compensate for too little chart space or long value labels.
title: Default

description: Place categories on the x-axis and values on the y-axis, where bar height represents value magnitude. Vertical bar charts work well for chronological trends and smaller category sets, and make differences in magnitude easy to compare.
title: Vertical

description: Place categories on the y-axis and values on the x-axis, where bar length represents value magnitude. Horizontal bar charts are best suited for:- Long category labels: Provides ample horizontal room for text, avoiding overlapping, truncation, or awkward label rotations.- Large datasets: Scales cleanly for 10 or more categories without compressing bar widths.- Rankings: Naturally presents ordered lists (ascending or descending) in a top-to-bottom reading flow.
title: Horizontal

description: Use min and max on the value axis to set explicit scale boundaries. Fixed ranges help standardize comparisons across charts, anchor benchmarks such as 0–100%, provide headroom for labels and tooltips, and prevent scale shifts when data changes. For stacked bar charts, account for the combined totals of the stacked series in each category so the full stacks fit within the scale.
title: Fixed Value Range

description: Bar charts can show negative values such as deficits, losses, or decreases. Bars extend away from the zero baseline. In stacked bar charts, negative values stack together below the zero baseline, separately from positive values.
title: Negative Values

description: Bar charts can combine positive and negative values to show gains and losses or deviations from a baseline. Bars extend in opposite directions from zero. In stacked bar charts, positive and negative values accumulate separately on their respective sides of the zero baseline.
title: Positive And Negative

description: Set barWidth to control bar thickness. A number specifies a fixed width in pixels, while a percentage string sets the width relative to the available category space and adapts to the chart size. By default, bars are responsive but capped at 24 px by the theme's barMaxWidth setting. To use bars wider than 24 px, also increase barMaxWidth on the series.
title: Custom Bar Width

description: Bar series use the chart's categorical palette by default. Use the color option to apply explicit colors to individual series.
title: Custom Colors

description: Depending on your use case, choose a categorical palette (up to 12 colors) or a sequential palette (recommended for up to 3 colors).
title: Categorical Vs Sequential

description: Enable a tooltip to inspect bar values on hover. For bar series it is recommended to set tooltip.axisPointer.type to 'shadow' to highlight the corresponding category and compare its values across series.
title: Tooltip

description: Use legendShow() to display a legend for named series. Series names become the legend labels, and users can toggle series visibility interactively.
title: Legend

description: Selection is disabled by default. Set selectedMode to true or 'single' to select one data item at a time, 'multiple' to select multiple data items, or 'series' to select an entire series.
title: Selected Mode

description: Configure a bullet chart via the chart config with type: 'synBullet' or with the seriesBullet preset function. Each data item requires numeric start, end and current values: the range extends from start to end and the marker shows current, which can be inside or outside the range. Range thickness adapts to the available category space and is capped by barMaxWidth by default.
title: Default

description: Place categories on the x-axis and values on the y-axis to compare actual values with their reference ranges vertically. This orientation works well for a small number of categories.
title: Vertical

description: Use colorBy: 'data' to assign range colors by item or colorBy: 'series' to give the items in a series the same color.
title: Color By

description: Place categories on the y-axis and values on the x-axis. Horizontal bullets provide more room for category labels and can be useful for compact KPI dashboards.
title: Horizontal

description: Use the palette attribute to apply another Synergy chart color palette to the bullet series.
title: Palette Colors

description: Set itemStyle on the series or on individual data items to customize range colors, border or shadows. Use Synergy chart tokens and keep the actual-value marker distinguishable from the range.
title: Custom Style

description: Enable a tooltip to inspect the range and actual value on hover. Set a name on each data item to show it in the tooltip. Without a name, the category label is used instead. Set tooltip.axisPointer.type to 'shadow' to highlight the corresponding category and compare values across series.
title: Tooltip

description: Show a legend for named bullet items so users can identify ranges and toggle individual items.
title: Legend Selection

description: Set min and max on the value axis to keep the scale consistent across charts or updates. Include the relevant range endpoints and actual values so they remain visible.
title: Fixed Axis Range

description: Set barWidth to control the thickness of the bullet range. A number specifies a fixed width in pixels, while a percentage string sets the width relative to the category band and adapts to the chart size. By default, ranges are responsive but capped at 24 px by the theme's barMaxWidth setting. To use ranges wider than 24 px, increase barMaxWidth on the series or explicitly set barMaxWidth: undefined in the initial series configuration to remove the maximum. Explicit barWidth ignores barCategoryGap and remains subject to barMinWidth.
title: Custom Range Width

description: Use markerStyle to set the actual-value marker's color, border, opacity, width and height. Width and height are physical pixel dimensions independent of orientation, the marker remains centered on the actual value.
title: Custom Marker

description: The donut chart can either be configured via config with type: 'synDonut' or with the seriesDonut preset function.
title: Default

description: By default, each outer ring segment is assigned a color from the chart's categorical color palette. Use the colors option to provide explicit colors instead; colors are repeated cyclically when fewer colors than data points are provided.
title: Custom Colors

description: Use the label property in the data items to apply custom label formatting. This can be a string or a function that receives the segment value and returns a formatted label. If the label is not set, the value will be used as the label. To omit the label completely, set the label to undefined.
title: Label Formatting

description: Use the label option to render a label for each segment, aligned by index with data. Each label is centered on its segment and placed outside the outer ring; provide a prefixIcon data URL alongside the label to render an icon before the label.
title: Labels With Icons

description: Use the radius option to define the donut's outer radius. The value can be specified either as a number (for a fixed pixel value, e.g. 20) or as a percentage string (e.g. '50%'). Percentage-based values automatically scale with the available space, while pixel values remain fixed.
title: Radius

description: Use the center option to position the donut inside the available layout area. Values can be pixels or percentages.
title: Adjust Center Position

description: Use top, right, bottom, and left to reduce the donut layout area from each side before center and radius are resolved. Insets can be set in pixels (number) or percentages (string).
title: Insets

description: Use legendShow() to render legend entries for the donut segments. Segment names are used as legend labels and can be toggled interactively. For this use the name option in the data items.
title: With Legend

description: Use tooltipShow() to display a segment's value on hover. Set a name on each data item to identify it in the tooltip. The synDonut series supports only trigger: 'item', which is set by default for the series, trigger: 'axis' does not work.
title: Tooltip

description: Use status colors to visualize the distribution of items across different statuses, such as error, warning, success, and neutral.
title: Status Donut

description: The gauge chart can either be configured via config with type: 'synGauge' or with the seriesGauge preset function.
title: Default

description: The gauge series supports showing an outer sections ring. Use sections.show: true together with sections.boundaries or sections.colors to render a color-coded outer ring around the gauge, where each adjacent pair of boundary values defines a segment. When no progressColor is set, the progress arc automatically adopts the color of the segment containing the current value.
title: Sections

description: Use trend.show: true together with trend.value to render a small pill trend indicator above the gauge value; set trend.direction to 'up' (default) or 'down' to control the directional icon, and optionally provide trend.iconUp or trend.iconDown with a custom data URL to replace the default icons.
title: Trend Indicator

description: Use the icon option to render an SVG image below the unit label, or below the value when no unit is set.
title: Icon

description: The gauge series supports custom value formatting using formatter.value, formatter.min, and formatter.max options.
title: Value Formatting

description: Configure a histogram with a series of type: 'bar' and set barMaxWidth to '100%' to let bars fill the available category space or use the seriesHistogram preset for the recommended configuration.
title: Default

description: A vertical histogram displays value intervals along the x-axis and their frequencies along the y-axis. This orientation is commonly used when there is sufficient horizontal space and makes it easy to compare the distribution across value ranges.
title: Vertical

description: A horizontal histogram displays value intervals along the y-axis and their frequencies along the x-axis. This orientation can improve readability when interval labels are long or when vertical space is more limited.
title: Horizontal

description: Use min and max on the value axis to set explicit scale boundaries. This ensures the axis scale remains consistent across datasets, making it easier to compare multiple charts and monitor changes over time.
title: Fixed Value Range

description: A histogram can show negative values such as losses, deficits or decreases. Bars extend below the zero baseline to represent the frequency of values within negative ranges.
title: Negative Values

description: A histogram can be used to visualize the distribution of positive and negative changes around a reference value. Negative bars represent decreases or values below the reference, while positive bars indicate increases or values above it.
title: Positive And Negative

description: Set barWidth to control bar thickness. A number specifies a fixed width in pixels, while a percentage string sets the width relative to the available category space and adapts to the chart size. Histograms are typically displayed with little or no gap between bars to emphasize the continuity of the underlying distribution. When barWidth is set, barCategoryGap is ignored.
title: Custom Bar Width

description: Set barCategoryGap to 0 to remove the gap between histogram bars, emphasizing the continuity of the distribution.
title: No Gap

description: Bar series use the chart's categorical palette by default. Use the color option to apply explicit colors to individual series.
title: Custom Colors

description: Enable a tooltip to inspect bar values on hover. For bar series it is recommended to set tooltip.axisPointer.type to 'shadow' to highlight the corresponding category and compare its values across series.
title: Tooltip

description: A histogram summarizes large datasets by grouping values into bins. In image processing, the bins can represent grayscale intensities from 0 (black) to 255 (white), and each bar shows the number of pixels at that intensity.
title: Large Data Set

description: The line chart can be configured with the seriesLine preset function.
title: Default

description: The line series supports curved lines. Use the smooth property to enable smooth curves for the line series.
title: Curved Line

description: The lines of line series can be hidden. When hidden, only the symbols remain, which is useful for minimal or simplified data displays.
title: Hidden Line

description: The line series supports a variety of styles, including line width and line type (solid, dashed, dotted). When combining multiple line charts, ensure there’s sufficient visual differentiation, for example, by using distinct line styles.
title: Multiple Line Styles

description: The line widths and symbol sizes can be adjusted to the needs.
title: Multiple Line Widths And Symbol Sizes

description: The line series supports a variety of symbols.
title: Multiple Symbol Styles

description: The tooltip provides contextual information when users hover or focus on data points within a chart. It displays values, labels without obstructing the view of the visualization. Use the tooltipShow preset to enable the tooltip.
title: Tooltip

description: Line charts can display both positive and negative values.
title: Positive And Negative Values

description: The segment chart can be configured via the chart config with type: 'synSegment' or with the seriesSegment preset function.
title: Default

description: The name option sets the name of the segment chart, which is displayed in the gap of the chart when provided. The text styling can be overwritten via nameTextStyle. It can be used to e.g. change the appearance like color, overflow handling, positioning and other text-related properties.
title: Name

description: By default, each segment item is assigned a color from the chart's categorical color palette. Use the colors option to provide explicit colors instead; colors are repeated cyclically when fewer colors than data points are provided.
title: Custom Colors

description: Segment labels can be provided as strings or formatter functions. If no label is provided, the value is used by default; set label to undefined to omit a label.
title: Label Formatting

description: Use the gap option to set the size of the open section in the segment ring. It is defined as a fraction of the full circle (0–1) and defaults to 0.3. Use gapOrientation to rotate the opening around the chart. By default, it is centered at the bottom.
title: Gap

description: Set gap to 0 to render no gap between the segments. Additionally a custom icon can be added to the inner circle via icon option.
title: No Gap

description: Use the min and max options to define the value range for the segment chart. This is useful when values share a known scale, such as a range from 0 to 1.
title: Min Max

description: Use the weight option on data items to control the relative width of each segment independently of its value. Segments without an explicit weight use the default weight.
title: Weights

description: Customize individual segments with itemStyle, backgroundStyle and labelTextStyle. Both backgroundStyle and itemStyle can be either set on chart or on data item level, labelTextStyle can only be set to the data item level. The chart level styling is inherited by all segments, while on the data item level it overrides the chart level styling for that specific segment.
title: Custom Styling

description: Use top, right, bottom, and left to reduce the segment layout area from each side before segment rendering is done. Insets can be set in pixels (number) or percentages (string).
title: Insets

description: Use legendShow() to display a legend for segment data items. Set the name option on each item to provide its legend label.
title: With Legend

description: Use tooltipShow() to display a segment's value on hover. Set a name on each data item to identify it in the tooltip. The synSegment series supports only trigger: 'item', which is set by default for the series, trigger: 'axis' does not work.
title: Tooltip
